issues: This is a substantive UNNUMBERED ninth-house introduction on original PDF640, not printed numbered CXXXIX. The printed chapter starts after the introduction on the SAME PDF640, so chapter numbering must not advance.
Though heading says 'Journeys and Religions', the substantive passage introduces only travel; no religious behavior or conviction claims are established by this particular source.
Lilly names ninth and its ruler, ninth occupants, Moon and Mercury, and attributes Mars addition to Ptolemy; exact original glyph and Ptolemy text have not been independently collated.
Travel yes/no, once/multiple times, frequent, nearly lifelong transmarine residence and rare foreign journeys are overlapping outcomes without a count threshold or defined observation age.
The author's destination question is conditional on already having decided travel will occur; it uses region relative to the natal country and allows several regions or a preferred one.
Principal causes of travel, travel success and life-threatening hazard are distinct dependent variable questions, not independently verified positive astrological examples.
The source provides no map projection, numeric bearing or physical distance, real-life case locations, journey registries, age horizons or comparable nonastrology baseline.
Speculations on death, travel danger and faith could cause harm and cannot be used as a present-day safety, religion or life forecast.
Historical source notes record what the 1647 author asks an astrologer to examine, NOT demonstrated answers or forecast accuracy.
The passage is source-anchored selective paraphrase and image provenance, not diplomatic seventeenth-century printed text edition.
